_: HISTORY below (2026-09-28 .. M5b-S3). The sectors after the capital are data/w2-lights' (owner, 2026-10-08): see the sector objects' own notes and docs/plans/w2-lights.md; the prose that follows does not describe them.
Level 1, re-authored 2026-09-28 under owner decision 8 (plan section 11):
Raider and Bomber waves ALTERNATE across the whole level. One WaveDef names
one archetype and the core page holds twenty of them, so the alternation is
per WAVE, not per formation - the owner's accepted equivalent. The retired
smoke scheduler alternated on every admission; the 'mixed wave' bit that
would express that in data is backlog, deliberately not implemented.
The twenty waves alternate R,B,R,B,... with no repeat anywhere, INCLUDING
across the sector boundary - which is what the first authoring got wrong.
The Director arms one wave at a time and a sector entry resets the cursor,
so a wave list that the row clock cuts short is abandoned where the cut
falls. When the cut falls before the LAST wave of a sector, the sector's
last-admitted archetype is no longer the authored one and the next sector's
first wave can repeat it: that is how 68b5968 produced twelve consecutive
Raider formations on HARD and twelve consecutive Bombers on EASY.
The two post-capital sectors are therefore SIZED for that, not split evenly:
* sector 3 is 856 rows and carries 5 waves of 6. The four waves before its
last total 24 formations, which every difficulty admits inside 856 rows
(EASY, the slowest stream, needs ~30 rows a formation), so the fifth wave
ALWAYS arms and the cut can only fall inside it. The sector's last
archetype is the authored one on all three difficulties;
* sector 4 is 2,040 rows - the format's maximum for one byte of modules -
and carries the other 13 waves. It is the LAST sector, so its own cut has
no successor to collide with, and it absorbs the whole difficulty spread:
HARD admits all 78 of its formations, MEDIUM 72, EASY what 9,000 frames
reach. 856 + 2,040 = 2,896 rows, the two sectors' old total, so the level
still ends on row 3,710 and the level-complete frame does not move.
Unchanged from the step-2 authoring, and pinned: sector 1 runs 272 rows so
the capital becomes due on the row MEDIUM reached at active frame 600
(owner decision 3); the capital traversal is 542 rows; seed 109 is $6D, so
all three RNG streams are the ones the game always had; spacing 24 is the
Heavy class floor, which leaves the kernel's admission retry (48/36/24
frames by difficulty) pacing the stream.
Sector 1 is left exactly as step 2 authored it - 4 + 4 formations on rows 0
and 88. Raising it to 5 + 5 puts the pre-capital count back on the ten that
main 28bd1e7 measured, and it was measured here, but it also moves the third
kill and with it the first weapon capsule, which three native pickup replays
script themselves around. The alternation does not need it, so it is not
taken: the level's own Heavy counts come out CLOSER to the baseline without
it (MEDIUM lands exactly on 109).
'entry' is the Light stepper's entry column. A Heavy formation takes its
columns from the renderer (88/152 Raider, 48/176 Bomber) and its Wingman
escort has always entered at 124, so every Heavy wave states 124 rather
than a column the runtime does not read.
MEASURED with scripts/level-timeline.mjs on this build, 9,000 frames, all
three difficulties - Heavy formations (pre-step-2 baseline in brackets) and
the longest run of one archetype:
EASY   100 (99)   longest run 6    MEDIUM 109 (109)  longest run 6
HARD   116 (122)  longest run 6
capital admits MEDIUM frame 606 row 272; level complete MEDIUM 8,249,
HARD 7,424 - all four unmoved from what step 2 measured.
A longest run of 6 is the floor the format allows at this density: 20 waves
of one archetype each must cover 116 formations.
PAYLOAD, roadmap 4.6 step 5 (docs/plans/director-4.6.md §8.3, owner decision
2026-10-01: a modest, player-visible use, waves unchanged). Two things only:
* THE SKY, one rule for every level: the capital sector flies under the
allied steel, the level's last sector under yellow, every other sector
under white. Level 1: white, steel, white, yellow. The colour is the
near-star pixel value and changes on the frame the Director enters the
sector - COLPF0, COLPF1 or COLPF2, no palette register is touched.
* ONE re-skinned Light, in ONE wave: sector 3's last wave (row 576), the
Raider + Wingman wave this file sizes so that it always arms on every
difficulty. Its Wingman escorts wear 'flight-lead' - the same red V with
white wingtips and a white nose. A Heavy wave's appearance re-skins its
Light escort; the Raiders keep their PMG art. Behaviour, HP, fire and
score are the Wingman's: a look is not an archetype (decision AD).
Level 1 authors no weapon look: its hostile fire is the default PULSE,
LASER and BOMBER.
M5b-S3: a fifth sector, the BOSS (region 1's Bastion, assets/graphics/boss-region-1.json).
Sectors 1-4 are unchanged, so every replay is main's up to the boss entry; sector 4 keeps

sectors._w2: data/w2-lights (owner answers of 2026-10-08, docs/plans/w2-lights.md §4.1, §8.1): the swarm after the capital - a Wingman column of three in the flight-lead look (Q2: the level's one re-skin moves here from P2's Raider escort), then three Interceptors closing on the player; up to three Lights at once (the swarm ceiling), no Heavy. The Interceptors come last because a Light wave holds the cursor until its last Light has gone and they live 116 frames to the column's 232, so the sector ends on its shortest Lights. 280 rows: with no kills its last Light is gone at its frame 461 on every difficulty and HARD's 280 rows last 560, a 21 % reserve (PROBE), so the elite sector after it opens on an empty playfield - the sector end is not a barrier (plan §3, F2). A swarm never follows an elite sector (F1; tests/level-one-waves.test.mjs, until C1).
sectors._flow: feat/sector-flow (owner, 2026-10-08; docs/plans/sector-flow.md): the sector ends as soon as its three waves are spent and the field is clear, so its rows are only the no-kill cut, and C1 holds the end while more Lights live than the elite sector after it admits. A third wave chained on (owner answer): a plain Wingman column down the other side (X 88) after the Interceptors. 384 rows: with no kills the last Light leaves at frame 759-760 after entry on every difficulty and HARD's 384 rows last 768 (PROBE, scripts/level-timeline.mjs lightTicksFromSector); the W2 reserve is gone - C1 replaces it.

sectors._w2: Variant (a) (owner decision a/b, 2026-10-08, docs/plans/director-4.6.md §11 item 20): a Raider pair with an Interceptor companion, which flies free from its admission and chases the player. With no kills the pair lives 334 frames, longer than these 240-300, and may cross into the Bomber sector: elite to elite, legal on both sides.

P2's Bomber sector, unchanged by data/w2-lights (scope 3) but for its place and its sky: one Bomber pair at row 24, after (a)'s Raiders, between the two Raider variants so the Heavy waves alternate (owner decision 8); white now that (b) is the last space sector.
sectors._flow: feat/sector-flow: the Bomber wave moves from row 24 to row 0 with afterCleared - it arms as soon as (a)'s Raider pair and its Interceptor are gone instead of after a fixed 24-row lead-in. 224 rows unchanged: with no kills (a)'s pair is carried in (elite to elite is legal) and the Bombers follow it.

sectors._w2: Variant (b): Raiders with no Light; the sector admits none (lights 0). A Raider with a Wingman escort, the third option, is sector 0's. It comes AFTER the Bomber pair so the Heavy waves still alternate (owner decision 8; the owner's answer of 2026-10-08, docs/plans/w2-lights.md §8.1). 240 rows: if the player kills nothing the Bomber pair can live into this sector, and its Raiders then arrive up to frame 394 of HARD's 480 (PROBE), a 22 % reserve.
